mechanical.match: Use when the task is one command to run and one output to read, and the deliverable is what it said: run the tests, read the log, report the failure. Not for finding where something lives.
mechanical.why: One command, one log, one named file. Report what it said and decide nothing.

reading.match: Use when a few files have to be understood before the answer can be given: read the diff, read the stack trace, read the failing test. Not for a change that has to be made.
reading.why: A few files that have to be understood before answering. A diff, a stack trace, a failing test name.

judgement.match: Use when a decision has consequences and the options are several: which design to take, why a subsystem breaks, which of these two layouts to keep. Not for carrying out a change that is already decided.
judgement.why: A decision with consequences: which of several designs to take, or why a subsystem breaks.

deep.match: Use when the work spans a whole subsystem, or the task is the word refactor. Not for a question with one answer.
deep.why: A whole subsystem, or the word refactor. The top of the ladder, and the most expensive tier in it.
